fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display against background clutter is a recognized driver-detection issue with direct stop-decision consequences during pedestrian crossings, substantive for a final-design-stage audit.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time background elements) is directly supported by the verbatim EV-US-001 quote citing Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a categorical safety_concern with no normative_basis_note, keeping it distinct from any MUTCD compliance question per FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border around the HAWK head is specific, located, actionable, and a viable established treatment for signal-head discrimination against clutter.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians explicitly identified as the exposed road users if drivers misread or detect the beacon late, tying driver conspicuity to VRU protection.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance interval adequacy for slower walkers at six high-collision-frequency HAWK sites is a genuine final-design-stage signal timing safety issue with real conflict-release exposure.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is backed by verbatim quote from EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians.') plus recorded TABLE A.10 Issue 2 provenance for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern about timing adequacy rather than a MUTCD compliance assertion, consistent with FHWA RSA semantics at final design stage.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all six named sites), actionable (reprogramme timings), and viable via standard reduced assumed walking speed practice; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians explicitly named as affected road users and the scenario centers on their crossing exposure, fully addressing VRU impact.
